scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Ukusina originates from South Africa's coastal region among the Zulu people.
The etymology stems from the verb sina ('to dance') and the prefix uku-.
Passed down primarily through oral traditions, the dance has been actively preserved and promoted against modernization through cultural festivals and institutions.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Ukusina is performed at weddings, memorial services, and coming-of-age ceremonies.
It serves as a spiritual ritual to communicate with ancestors and request blessings, alongside its role in social entertainment.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance features tremendous dexterity and vigor, led by an induna who sets the pace.
Movements include powerful leg kicks in any direction up and out, ground-stamping of each foot, hops, and deft hand movements performed in line or circular patterns.
Watch for Ukusina Leg Kick and Stamp.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Performances are socially created around a song leader singing interlocking word phrases.
The rhythmic foundation is provided by traditional Zulu drums and other percussion instruments.
Listen for the traditional Zulu drums, percussion instruments.
Traditional Zulu drums and percussion establish a steady rhythmic beat, complemented by a song leader singing interlocking word phrases.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers wear intricate beadwork on headdresses, necklaces, bracelets, and anklets, alongside animal-skin clothing from cows and goats and spiritual feathers.
Men wear an ibheshu or isikhakha, while women wear an isidwaba.
